citation.authors: Aloia J, Fazzari M, Islam S, Mikhail M et al
citation.journal: Journal of Bone and Mineral Research

record.population: 260 healthy Black American women aged 60 or over
record.design: Randomised, double-dummy, placebo-controlled, 3 years, vitamin D3 dose adjusted to keep blood level above 75 nmol/L
record.finding: No bone-loss benefit of vitamin D over placebo; the groups were equivalent. Baseline 25(OH)D was 54.8 nmol/L. The authors concluded that Black Americans should have the same vitamin D exposure as White Americans.
